question: In the eighteenth century, where did the Sikh community gather during Baisakhi and Diwali to take collective decisions called Gurmatas?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Amritsar**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• During the **eighteenth century**, the **Sikh community** gathered in **Amritsar** during the festivals of **Baisakhi** and **Diwali** to take collective decisions known as **Gurmatas**. 
• The **Gurmata** was a form of deliberative assembly among the Sikhs, where important communal and political decisions were taken collectively by the community leaders. 
• **Amritsar**, being a major religious and cultural center for Sikhs, served as the focal point for such gatherings, especially at the **Golden Temple**. 
• These decisions, called **Gurmatas**, were binding on the entire Sikh community and often pertained to critical matters like military strategy, religious issues, and governance. 
• The practice of holding Gurmatas in Amritsar highlights the city’s importance as the spiritual and political heart of the Sikh community during that period. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 
• **Gurmata:** 
• The term **Gurmata** translates to "Guru’s decision" and refers to resolutions passed during Sikh gatherings. 
• These decisions were considered sacred and of utmost importance, as they were believed to be guided by divine will. 
• Gurmatas played a significant role in uniting the Sikh community and addressing both internal and external challenges during the turbulent eighteenth century. 
• **Amritsar:** 
• Amritsar is one of the holiest cities for Sikhs and is home to the **Golden Temple**, also known as **Harmandir Sahib**. 
• It was founded in the **16th century by Guru Ram Das**, the fourth Sikh Guru, and became the epicenter of Sikhism. 
• The city hosted important Sikh gatherings, especially during the festivals of **Baisakhi** and **Diwali**. 
• **Baisakhi:** 
• **Baisakhi** is a major Sikh festival that marks the **harvest season** and the establishment of the **Khalsa Panth** in 1699 by Guru Gobind Singh Ji. 
• It is celebrated with great enthusiasm and is one of the key occasions for the Sikh community to gather and discuss matters of importance. 
• **Diwali and Sikhs:** 
• For Sikhs, **Diwali** holds special significance as it marks the release of the sixth Guru, **Guru Hargobind Ji**, from captivity in 1619. 
• It is also a time for the community to come together, commemorate historical events, and make collective decisions. 
• **Historical Importance of Sikh Assemblies:** 
• Such assemblies contributed to the strengthening of Sikh unity and allowed the community to respond collectively to external threats, especially during the Mughal period and invasions by Afghan rulers. 
• The resolutions passed during these gatherings often had far-reaching impacts on Sikh governance and military strategies.
